title: HighWave: Large-Scale High-Bandwidth Wave Simulations on FPGAs
problem: Wave simulations represented as PDEs face memory bandwidth bottlenecks on FPGAs, especially when using discontinuous Galerkin schemes with low arithmetic intensity and complex irregular data access patterns. Achieving high HBM utilization while managing irregular accesses requires careful co-design of compute and memory systems.
motivation: Wave simulations are critical across HPC domains, and FPGAs offer reconfigurable hardware for application-specific optimization with significantly lower power than GPUs, but their memory systems must be specialized to handle irregular access patterns efficiently.
method: HighWave employs a spatial FPGA architecture with configurable processing cores that integrate High-Bandwidth Memory through coordinated memory optimizations. The design maximizes data reuse, minimizes access irregularities through careful scheduling, and ensures load balancing across memory channels. It targets discontinuous Galerkin wave solvers with Gauss-Lobatto-Legendre quadrature and supports elastic and acoustic wave equations.
key_novelty: First FPGA wave simulator with HBM integration and co-designed memory optimizations (data reuse, irregular access mitigation, load balancing) achieving high bandwidth utilization for intrinsically low-arithmetic-intensity discontinuous Galerkin schemes.
contributions: HighWave: scalable FPGA spatial architecture with HBM integration for wave simulations
Memory optimization techniques (data reuse, irregular access handling, load balancing) for discontinuous Galerkin solvers
Better scalability for cluster-level deployment compared to prior FPGA wave accelerators
72.2% HBM bandwidth utilization with 48% higher performance and 2.84x better energy efficiency than Nvidia V100

metrics.speedup: 48% higher performance than Nvidia V100 (normalized for equivalent peak bandwidth)

limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations, scalability constraints, or generalization to other PDE types beyond elastic and acoustic wave equations.
primary_theme: Memory-optimized FPGA acceleration for wave PDEs via HBM integration
